events.subtitle: Japan Tour 2026 — Breathe release tour
events.category: Japan / Contemporary acoustic jazz / Piano trio
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents the Miki Yamanaka Piano Trio on Monday, October 19, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The official event page identifies Miki Yamanaka on piano, Tyrone Allen on bass, and Jimmy Macbride on drums, describes Allen and Macbride as Yamanaka's regular trio partners, and frames the Tokyo engagement as part of the Japan tour for her new album Breathe. Breathe was released on August 14, 2026; the recording includes Yamanaka, Allen and Macbride, with Nicole Glover added on saxophones and spoken word.

en.why_it_matters: This belongs on RADAR because it catches a Japanese pianist whose working language was built in New York bringing her regular trio back into a Tokyo club around music that has just been released. Allen and Macbride are not anonymous support: they are the rhythm section Yamanaka describes as a tightly integrated regular trio, and Breathe gives the date a current compositional center rather than a generic standards-night rationale. The appeal is the piano-trio conversation itself — touch, time, harmonic movement and how a band that works together in New York changes when that language lands in Tokyo.
en.trip_verdict: Keep it on the board if October 19 is open in Tokyo. It is a strong night for contemporary acoustic jazz and a useful bridge between the New York and Japan threads, but I would fit it around rarer masters, premieres, reunions or one-off contexts rather than move one of those to make room.

es.why_it_matters: Ésta entra al RADAR porque captura a una pianista japonesa cuyo lenguaje de trabajo se formó en Nueva York regresando a un club de Tokio con su trío habitual y música recién publicada. Allen y Macbride no son acompañantes intercambiables: forman la sección rítmica estable con la que Yamanaka ha construido una conversación muy cerrada, y Breathe le da a la fecha un centro compositivo actual en vez de convertirla en otra noche genérica de standards. Lo interesante es justamente escuchar el trío —toque, tiempo, movimiento armónico y cómo cambia en Tokio una banda que se ha hecho trabajando en Nueva York.
es.trip_verdict: La tendría en el tablero si el 19 de octubre está libre en Tokio. Es una buena noche de jazz acústico contemporáneo y un puente natural entre los hilos Nueva York y Japón, pero la acomodaría alrededor de maestros más raros, estrenos, reuniones o contextos de una sola fecha en vez de desplazar uno de esos conciertos para hacerle espacio.
